text:
maria: Heads-up — we've got a cluster of SSE resume storms hitting the proxy circuit-breaker for a few tenants. Seen ~3x reconnects in 30s and the proxy is collapsing into 'coalesce' debounce which drops resume tokens.
ajay: ugh. Which breaker is tripping? per-tenant concurrency or global?
maria: Per-tenant, looks like the new session-guard in proxy v2 (cc @tyler). Logs show `circuit=tenant_conn_quota action=trip reason=rapid_connects window=27s` then `resume_token_invalidated` for a subset.
tyler: I pushed the guard to reduce noisy fanout, but it sounds like we're conflating resume attempts with fresh sessions. If client does fast reconnect (backoff jitter=200-800ms) proxy counts them as new.
elin: Console telemetry shows spike in "resume_failure" alerts and downstream billing duplication flags. Dashboards show tokens marked as replayed then evicted.
ajay: Can we just treat resume requests that present a valid resume_id and have last_seen < X seconds as idempotent and exempt from breaker?
maria: That's my read. Current implementation increments active_sessions before resume validation. If validation fails we end up evicting kvcache and the client restarts from scratch -> duplicate billing & lost context.
tyler: Agreed. Quick fix: move resume validation earlier in the proxy flow so we only increment count after resume accepted. Longer term: add a tiny state machine so resume attempts acquire a light-weight allowlist entry for 2s.
elin: Also observed that coalescing debounce merges heartbeats and masks missed pings — console shows fewer heartbeats than client; sampling is misleading. We should emit a "resume_attempt" event metric.
ops-bot: deploy-started: proxy v2.1.3-rollout canary to 3 hosts in us-west.
ajay: For immediate mitigation, can we lower the aggressiveness of the breaker threshold for tiered-test tenants? e.g., from 15 connects/s to 50/s for canary group?
maria: I don't want to weaken breaker globally. Suggest route: 1) hotfix proxy to validate resume_token before counting 2) add metric `sse.resume.attempt` with tags {tenant, outcome} 3) console viz for resume success rate + kvcache evict count 4) rollout to canary.
tyler: I'll open PR for (1) and add unit tests covering resume race where two rapid connects present same resume_id. Patch will be small.
elin: For dashboards, we need an alert: "resume_success_rate < 90% over 5m" and link to kvcache eviction trace. Right now alerts are tied to disconnect count which is noisy.
ajay: Operator UX: when the breaker trips, console should show sample session ids that caused the trip (anonymized) instead of just tenant id. Makes root cause much faster.
maria: Good idea — add sample_session_ids to the circuit-breaker trace event (hashed). Low-cardinality.
tyler: One more edge: some clients auto-retry with exponential backoff but use same TCP connection keepalive disabled; the proxy sees TCP reconnects as separate. We should document recommended client behavior: keepalive + jitter > 500ms. I'll add a short doc blurb in devex.
elin: Ok plan of record: Tyler lands resume-validate-first hotfix -> deploy canary -> emit new metrics -> add console panels & alert -> monitor for billing dupes.
ajay: I'll coordinate canary tenants and temporarily relax tenant breaker for them.
maria: I'll file an incident note and set the postmortem template. Add links to traces: https://console/replay/trace/4312345678 (sample)
tyler: PR: https://github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/845 (draft) — tests included.
ops-bot: deploy-success: proxy v2.1.3-rollout canary (3 hosts) completed in us-west after 4m.
elin: Initial canary looks good — resume_success rate jumped from 62% -> 96% for the flagged tenants. No billing duplicates in 15m sample.
maria: Great. Follow-ups: add alert, doc, and do a wider rollout next week with postmortem. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
